subject: ophthalmology
title: Physiology of vision: acuity, colour, and retinal function

steps.tx: Visual acuity is tested with a **Snellen chart** placed at 6 metres. A letter that subtends 5 minutes of arc at the nodal point is read at 6/6, meaning the patient sees at 6 metres what a normal eye sees at 6 metres. The **LogMAR** scale is the research-preferred alternative. The breadth of each stroke subtends 1 minute of arc, and the whole letter subtends 5 minutes.

steps.tx: Colour vision is tested mainly with **Ishihara plates**, which screen for **red-green** defects. The Farnsworth-Munsell 100 hue test is the most sensitive test for congenital and acquired defects. The Hardy-Rand-Ritler plates detect blue-yellow anomalies. The Nagel anomaloscope quantifies red-green mixing.

steps.tx: Colour sensation arises from **cones** in photopic vision. Normal colour vision is **trichromatic**, the basis of the Young-Helmholtz theory. Rods do not mediate colour. The **rhodopsin** cycle begins when light converts 11-cis retinal to all-trans retinal, which then dissociates from opsin. Regeneration of rhodopsin is the **visual cycle**.

steps.tx: The **electroretinogram** (ERG) records retinal potentials to a flash. The **a-wave** is negative and comes from photoreceptors. The **b-wave** is a large positive wave from bipolar cells, with Muller cells contributing. The **c-wave** reflects pigment epithelium activity in the dark-adapted eye. A flash ERG misses small macular lesions.
